To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) PLB-U and -N hold with high probability (almost surely) for several well-studied graph classes, (2) greedy algorithms can be used for constant-factor approximations of Minimum Vertex Cover, Minimum Dominating Set, and Maximum Independent Set on PLB graphs with $$\beta \in (2,3)$$ β ∈ ( 2, 3 ), and (3) these problems are AP X -hard and not in PTAS on PLB graphs.
the greedy approach works on deterministic PLB networks with $$\beta>2$$ β >2, and that the greedy approach does not work on deterministic PLB graphs with $$\beta\le 2$$ β ≤ 2.
the greedy approach achieves a constant-factor approximation if the network is scale-free and the power-law upper bound is sufficiently strong.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the structural properties that allow for efficient deterministic algorithms?
the following questions: Which random graph models satisfy the PLB properties?
the interplay of the PLB-U and the PLB-N properties, which we show to be sufficient for the greedy approach, but also necessary for a constant approximation ratio.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the greedy approach is the best we can hope for on PLB graphs.
the greedy approach is either optimal or at least close to optimal for Minimum Vertex Cover, Minimum Dominating Set, and Maximum Independent Set on PLB networks with $$\beta \in (2,3]$$ β ∈ ( 2, 3 ].
greedy approaches are very good on PLB graphs, but not good enough to achieve a PTAS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PLB properties are not sufficient to obtain polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTAS), but they do allow for constant-factor approximations.
the power-law behavior of real-world networks is not only beneficial for designing fast algorithms, but also helps to achieve constant-factor approximations for classical optimization problems.
the greedy approach is very powerful on deterministic scale-free networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PLB networks are a very rich and interesting class of networks.
the greedy algorithm is not only fast but also achieves good quality solutions for many real-world networks.
the PLB properties are sufficient for a constant-factor approximation by a greedy algorithm, but not necessary for a PTAS or APX-hardness.
